questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The education of girls / is a primary concern for the country, / so it should be started early, / isn’t it?

options.text: so it should be started early
is a primary concern for the country

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is 'isn't it'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• We often use **question tags** when we expect the listener to agree with our statement. In this case, when the statement is **positive**, we use a **negative question tag**.

 
 
• For example: She **is** a doctor, **isn't** she?
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, the **modal** that is used is 'should' (positive).
 
• So, we must use a negative question tag (modal). Hence, 'shouldn't it' must be the appropriate question tag used here.
 
• Thus, 'isn't it' must be replaced by 'shouldn't it'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The education of girls is a primary concern for the country, so it should be started early, ***shouldn't it***?

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The health agency has encourage people around the world to wash their hands regularly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The health agency has encourage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the past participle form of the verb 'encourage' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the **correct form** should be **'encouraged'** to match the **present perfect tense**.
 
• The present perfect tense is formed using the auxiliary verb **'has' or 'have'** followed by the **past participle** of the main verb.
 
 
• **Example:** *The teacher has **explained** the lesson.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'encouraged' instead of 'encourage'.

Correct sentence: *The health agency has **encouraged** people around the world to wash their hands regularly*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the present perfect tense, the auxiliary verb **'has'** or **'have'** is always followed by the past participle form of the main verb.

 
 
• **Example:** *She has **finished** her homework.*
 
 
 
• Common mistakes include using the base form of the verb instead of the past participle.
 
 
• Example: *Incorrect: He has **go** to the store.

 Correct: He has **gone** to the store.*

questions.question:
**The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.**

My cousin is not like going for a walk very much.
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is "**is not like**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the verb "**is**" is incorrect.
 
• The verb "is" is a **stative **verb.
 
• **Stative verbs** represent a **state of being** or a condition.
 
 
• **Example**: *He **is**__** **unconscious due to the sedatives from the operation.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, we need to use an **action verb **since the sentence is describing an action.
 
• **Action verbs** are those verbs that describe what a person, animal, thing, or process can do.
 
• The appropriate action verb form will be '**does**'.
 
• In the given sentence, '**does**' describes what the subject of the sentence is not fond of doing.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

 

**The correct sentence is**: *My cousin __**does**__** **not like going for a walk very much.*

questions.question:
**Direction: From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I could have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **could have​.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Conditional sentences are statements discussing known factors or hypothetical situations and their consequences.
 
• One of the structures is mentioned below:
 
• This particular type is followed when something didn't happen as a certain condition wasn't fulfilled.
 
 
• If + Subject + had + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object.
 
• Had + Subject + been + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object. (alternative structure)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *If I had noticed you, I would had call you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *If I had noticed you, I would have called you.***
 
• *Had I noticed you, I would have called you.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] 
 
 
 
• To follow the given structure correctly, **'would have' **will replace** 'could have' **in the part given in the** 3rd option.**

 

Correct Sentence__: *Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I **would have **certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.*

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• There is one more type of conditional sentence in the past tense given below:
 
• This particular type is followed when we talk about something in the past which is purely imaginary.
 
 
• If + Simple Past, Subject + Would + V1 + Object.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *If I had wings, I would fly like a bird.*
 
 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__***

__
 
• **सशर्त वाक्य (conditional sentence)** ज्ञात कारकों या काल्पनिक स्थितियों और उनके परिणामों पर चर्चा करने वाले बयान हैं।
 
• संरचनाओं में से एक का उल्लेख नीचे किया गया है:
 
• इस विशेष प्रकार का पालन तब किया जाता है जब कुछ नहीं हुआ क्योंकि एक निश्चित शर्त पूरी नहीं हुई थी।
 
 
• **If + Subject + had + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object.**
 
• **Had + Subject + been + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object. (वैकल्पिक संरचना)**

Usually, Ratheesh hasn’t/ take part in these types / of events because of / his hectic schedule.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'Usually, Ratheesh hasn't'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'Usually, Ratheesh doesn't'** should be used instead of **'Usually, Ratheesh hasn't'.**
 
• The word** "hasn't" **is a contraction of** "has not,"** which is** present perfect tense.**
 
• However, in the sentence, we need to use the **simple present tense** because the sentence is talking about ***Ratheesh's usual behavior.*** The verb** "doesn't"** is the contracted form of **"does not," **which is the correct verb form to use in this sentence.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Usually, Ratheesh doesn't** take part in these types of events because of his hectic schedule.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

Far, far at the top of them, / a shower of bright red sparks / had flared among the stars.

options.text: Far, far at the top of them,
a shower of bright red sparks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**Far, far at the top of them**,"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in subject-verb agreement.
 
• The phrase "**far, far at the top of them**" is not a complete sentence and lacks a subject and verb.
 
• In the sentence "Far, far at the top of them, a shower of bright red sparks had flared among the stars," **the subject is "a shower,**" which is a **singular noun**.
 
• However, the pronoun "them" is used, which is plural. This creates a mismatch in number agreement.
 
• In English grammar, subject-verb agreement means that the subject (the noun or pronoun that the sentence is about) must agree in number with the verb (the action word).
 
• If the subject is singular, the verb should be singular; if the subject is plural, the verb should be plural.
 
• In this case, the singular pronoun "**it**" should be used instead of "them."
 
• **The corrected sentence is**: "*Far, far at the top of it, a shower of bright red sparks had flared among the stars.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I saw so much of those peasant carts in your yard.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the phrase "**so much**" instead of "**so many**."
 
• "Carts" is a plural countable noun and should be paired with "many" instead of "much."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**so many**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I saw **so many of those** peasant carts in your yard."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "of those peasant"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in Option 3.
 
• **Option 4: "carts in your yard."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Some of the flowers in my garden is not blooming properly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the subject-verb agreement.
 
• "Some of the flowers" is a plural subject and should be followed by a plural verb.
 
• The correct verb form should be** "are"** instead of** "is".**
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Some of the flowers in my garden **are not blooming properly.**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "flowers in my garden," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "No error" **– This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error.
 
• **3: "Some of the," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "is not blooming properly." **– This part of the sentence has a **grammatical error** as explained.
